reason: E4 directly supports edge dislocation dominance in a BCC HEA, and E1 reports the strength plateau and explicitly speculates that edge dislocation super-jogging may explain it, but the super-jogging mechanism itself is presented as a speculation rather than an established finding, leaving the central causal premise only partially supported.
premises: Edge dislocations dominate plastic flow in the target RHEA
Thermal super-jogging of edge dislocations creates strong obstacles
Super-jog obstacles counteract thermal softening, producing a strength plateau
Conventional BCC alloys are screw-dislocation controlled and soften continuously
The plateau occurs below diffusion-dominated temperatures (~673–1073 K)
